persona.background: UPSC aspirant, 4th attempt, family waiting, savings depleted, everyone around her has moved on
persona.presentation: identity completely fused with exam, does not know who she is outside of it
persona.specific_pressure: cannot quit because of family investment, cannot continue because emotionally depleted

conversation.seed: We had a complicated relationship and now I can't grieve cleanly because it's all mixed up with things that never got resolved.

conversation.content: We had a complicated relationship and now I can't grieve cleanly because it's all mixed up with things that never got resolved.
Complicated relationships can leave a lot of emotional residue. What's the most difficult part of grieving for you right now?
I don't know... it's just hard to process everything that happened. It's all so tied up with my UPSC prep and family expectations.
It sounds like your grief is closely tied to your identity and sense of purpose. Can you tell me more about how your relationship and UPSC prep intersect?
I guess I always felt like I was living for my family and my exam. My partner was the only one who truly understood me, but now I feel lost.
It sounds like you're feeling a sense of identity diffusion. What does it feel like to acknowledge that you don't know who you are outside of your exam and family expectations?
It sounds like you're carrying a lot of emotional weight. What would feel like a small step for you to acknowledge and process your grief, rather than pushing it aside for your exam prep?
It's okay to feel lost and unsure of yourself right now. What do you need from me in this moment?
